hints: Rationalise the denominator by multiplying numerator and denominator by the conjugate $1+\sqrt3i$.
Expand using $i^2=-1$ and simplify the real denominator.
Separate the simplified numerator into its real and imaginary parts to write $u=x+iy$.
walkthrough: Start from the given complex number $u = \dfrac{4\mathrm{i}}{1 - (\sqrt{3})\mathrm{i}}$.

Multiply the numerator and denominator by the complex conjugate of the denominator, $(1 + \sqrt{3}\mathrm{i})$:
$$u = \dfrac{4\mathrm{i}(1 + \sqrt{3}\mathrm{i})}{(1 - \sqrt{3}\mathrm{i})(1 + \sqrt{3}\mathrm{i})}$$

Expand the denominator using $(a - b\mathrm{i})(a + b\mathrm{i}) = a^2 + b^2$:
$$(1 - \sqrt{3}\mathrm{i})(1 + \sqrt{3}\mathrm{i}) = 1^2 - (\sqrt{3}\mathrm{i})^2 = 1 - 3\mathrm{i}^2 = 1 - 3(-1) = 1 + 3 = 4$$

hints: Use the Cartesian form of $u$ from part (i) to find its modulus and quadrant.
The point lies in quadrant II with reference angle $\pi/6$, so express its principal argument exactly.
walkthrough:
Determine the argument of $u$:
Since the real part is $-\sqrt{3} < 0$ and the imaginary part is $1 > 0$, $u$ lies in the second quadrant:
$$\text{Basic acute angle } \alpha = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = \dfrac{1}{6}\pi$$
$$\arg(u) = \pi - \alpha = \pi - \dfrac{1}{6}\pi = \dfrac{5}{6}\pi \quad (\text{or } 150^\circ)$$

hints: Interpret $|z|<2$ as the interior of a circle centred at the origin, with the boundary excluded.
Plot $u=(-\sqrt3,1)$. The condition $|z-u|<|z|$ selects points closer to $u$ than to the origin.
Draw the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining $0$ to $u$ and choose its $u$-side.
Shade the intersection of that half-plane with the open disc, drawing both strict boundaries as excluded.
walkthrough: Plot the point $u = -\sqrt{3} + \mathrm{i}$ on the Argand diagram at coordinates $(-\sqrt{3}, 1)$. Note that $|u| = 2$, so $u$ lies on the circle of radius $2$ centered at the origin $O(0, 0)$.

Interpret the inequality $|z| < 2$:
- The boundary $|z| = 2$ is a circle centered at the origin with radius $2$.
- Because the inequality is strict ($< 2$), this boundary circle is drawn as a dashed (broken) line.
- The inequality represents the interior region of this circle.

Interpret the inequality $|z - u| < |z|$:
- The equation $|z - u| = |z|$ is the perpendicular bisector of the line segment joining the origin $O$ to $u$.
- The midpoint of segment $Ou$ has position vector $\dfrac{1}{2}u = -\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{i}$.
- The perpendicular bisector passes through this midpoint and is perpendicular to the line $Ou$.
- Because the inequality is strict, this line is drawn as a dashed (broken) line.
- The inequality $|z - u| < |z|$ represents the open half-plane of points that are closer to $u$ than to the origin.

Shade the intersection:
- Shade the region lying inside the dashed circle of radius $2$ and on the side of the dashed perpendicular bisector that contains $u$.
